nodes.name: Interleaving anomalies
nodes.statement: Databases run many transactions, groups of reads and writes treated as one unit, at the same time. Some interleavings of their steps produce results that no one-at-a-time order could produce.

nodes.name: Serializable execution
nodes.statement: A concurrent execution is serializable if its result equals the result of running the same transactions one at a time in some order.

nodes.name: Dirty read
nodes.statement: A dirty read happens when a transaction reads a value that another transaction wrote but has not committed. If the writer then aborts, the reader has used data that never officially existed.

nodes.name: Non-repeatable read
nodes.statement: A non-repeatable read happens when a transaction reads the same row twice and gets different values, because another transaction committed an update in between.

nodes.name: Phantom read
nodes.statement: A phantom happens when a transaction runs the same range query twice and gets a different set of rows, because another transaction inserted or deleted matching rows in between.

nodes.name: Lost update
nodes.statement: A lost update happens when two transactions read the same value, each computes a new value from it, and the second write silently replaces the first.

nodes.name: Write skew
nodes.statement: Write skew happens when two transactions read overlapping data and each updates a different row based on what it read. Together they break a rule that each one alone would have kept.

nodes.name: Levels defined by anomalies
nodes.statement: The SQL standard defines four isolation levels by which of three anomalies each one forbids: dirty reads, non-repeatable reads and phantoms.

nodes.name: Read Uncommitted
nodes.statement: The Read Uncommitted level permits dirty reads, non-repeatable reads and phantoms.

nodes.name: Read Committed
nodes.statement: The Read Committed level forbids dirty reads but permits non-repeatable reads and phantoms.

nodes.name: Repeatable Read
nodes.statement: In the SQL standard, the Repeatable Read level forbids dirty and non-repeatable reads but still permits phantoms.

nodes.name: Serializable level
nodes.statement: The standard's Serializable level forbids all three named anomalies and requires every result to match some serial order.

nodes.name: Gap in the standard
nodes.statement: Forbidding the three anomalies the standard names does not guarantee serializability, because anomalies such as write skew are not among them.

nodes.name: Read Committed loses updates
nodes.statement: Read Committed alone does not prevent lost updates, because both transactions read only committed data before either one writes.

nodes.name: Snapshot isolation
nodes.statement: Under snapshot isolation, each transaction reads from a consistent snapshot of the committed data as it stood when the transaction started.

nodes.name: First committer wins
nodes.statement: Under snapshot isolation, when two concurrent transactions write the same row, only the first to commit succeeds and the other is aborted.

nodes.name: Snapshots stop lost updates
nodes.statement: Snapshot isolation prevents lost updates, because the second transaction to write the same row is aborted instead of overwriting the first.

nodes.name: Snapshots stop read anomalies
nodes.statement: Snapshot isolation prevents dirty reads, non-repeatable reads and phantoms, because every read in a transaction uses the same committed snapshot.

nodes.name: Snapshots allow write skew
nodes.statement: Snapshot isolation permits write skew, because two transactions that update different rows never collide on a shared row.

nodes.name: Snapshot is not serializable
nodes.statement: Snapshot isolation is not serializable, even though it forbids all three anomalies that the SQL standard names.

nodes.name: On-call doctors
nodes.statement: Under snapshot isolation, two on-call doctors can each see that the other is still on call and both sign off at once. The hospital then has nobody on call.

nodes.name: PostgreSQL Repeatable Read
nodes.statement: PostgreSQL implements its Repeatable Read level with snapshot isolation, so it forbids phantoms that the standard would allow at that level.

nodes.name: Two-phase locking
nodes.statement: Under strict two-phase locking, a transaction holds its locks until it commits or aborts. Readers and writers of the same data block each other, and the database aborts one transaction to break a deadlock.

nodes.name: Range locks
nodes.statement: Locking a range or predicate, such as with next-key locks, stops other transactions from inserting or deleting rows that would match a query.

nodes.name: Locking gives serializability
nodes.statement: Strict two-phase locking combined with range locks produces only serializable executions, phantoms included.

nodes.name: Serializable snapshot isolation
nodes.statement: Serializable snapshot isolation keeps snapshot reads but tracks read-write dependencies between concurrent transactions. It aborts a transaction when those dependencies form a dangerous pattern, so every committed result is serializable.

nodes.name: Retrying aborted transactions
nodes.statement: Applications at the Serializable level must be ready to retry a transaction, because the database may abort it to break a deadlock or a serialization conflict.

nodes.name: The isolation trade-off
nodes.statement: Choosing an isolation level trades correctness for throughput. Weaker levels block and abort less often but allow more anomalies.
